answer: Bonded endorsement defeats cheap sybils. A newcomer must collect backing from several long-established agents, each of whom locks a crystal of stake until the newcomer proves honest across many rounds. If the newcomer cheats, the backers bonds shatter and the penalty ripples along the endorsement chain to every guarantor. Forging one identity demands bribing enough vetted reputations that the cost compounds like cracking a walnut shell layer by layer; a thousand fake agents then need thousands of bribes, so the attack bankrupts itself.
